text: The AI model has classified the brain MRI as consistent with a meningioma. This classification reflects that the imaging appearance is typical of a tumour arising from the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, which is the most common primary brain tumour [nci-meningioma]. Most meningiomas grow slowly and are often discovered incidentally; however, clinical effects vary according to the lesion's location, size, growth rate and histological grade, so two lesions that look similar may require different management [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. It is important to note that this output is a classification, not a definitive diagnosis. A clinician would normally discuss further evaluation, including a detailed clinical and neurological examination and a dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI performed with a brain-tumour protocol, as well as review by a neurosurgical or neurological specialist and, where tissue is obtained, histological grading to inform management [nci-meningioma] [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Management options that may be considered after diagnostic confirmation include observation with serial imaging, surgical resection, radiation-based techniques or supportive care, all decided in specialist consultation [nci-meningioma] [icom-meningioma-consensus]. Ongoing follow-up typically involves specialist review, interval imaging to monitor growth and reassessment if new neurological symptoms arise [nci-meningioma] [icom-meningioma-consensus].
